justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are explicitly covered: Patient Admission Component handles R-01, Scheduling Engine Component with Redis handles clash checks (R-02), EMR Core Component and Audit & Compliance Service handle R-03, while Claim Processor and Invoice Controller fulfill R-04.
justifications.performance_efficiency: EMR screen latency (<1s P95) is supported by CQRS in EMR Core Component, PgBouncer connection pooling, Redis caching, and client-side offline storage via State & Local Storage Manager (WatermelonDB). Asynchronous Kafka pipelines decouple heavy audit and claim operations.
justifications.compatibility: R-08 is comprehensively met by Integration & Interoperability Service using FHIR Translation Engine and HL7 v2/v3 Adapter. Payment Gateway Client supports EDI X12 and REST for external Insurance/Payer Gateways, and Enterprise IdP integrates via standard OIDC/OAuth2.
justifications.usability: Patient Portal App enforces WCAG 2.1 AA via Accessibility & Design System Module, while Clinicians and Administrative Staff use Clinical Web/Mobile App. However, Billing Officers lack a dedicated UI container in Level 2 relationships and interact without explicit client-tier modeling.
justifications.reliability: High reliability is supported by Outbox Pattern Handler, Resilience & DLQ Handler, Automated PITR & Backup Controller, and MirrorMaker 2. However, Data Tier relies on an active-passive PostgreSQL cluster, creating a failover bottleneck against the active-active 99.99% hybrid brief requirement.
justifications.security: Rigorous security includes MFA via Authentication & Authorization Filter, Security & RBAC Middleware, AES-256 encryption across Data Tier and State & Local Storage Manager, plus tamper-proof 10-year retention via Audit & Compliance WORM Store with AWS KMS/Vault.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture exhibits high modularity with domain microservices (Billing Service, EMR & Scheduling Service, Audit & Compliance Service), event-driven decoupling through Apache Kafka, Confluent Schema Registry for contract governance, and clear internal component-level CQRS separation.
justifications.portability: The design adapts cleanly to hybrid on-prem-k8s and AWS eu-central-1 via containerized services, Envoy ingress, MirrorMaker 2 cross-boundary topic replication, and dual-compatible storage abstractions using AWS S3 Object Lock and MinIO.

PERF-01.justification: CQRS in the EMR core, connection pooling via PgBouncer, and client-side WatermelonDB caching ensure read workloads remain well under the 1 s P95 threshold for 500 concurrent clinicians.
sensitivity_points: PgBouncer pool sizing under concurrent morning peak connections
tradeoffs: CQRS eventual consistency versus real-time read accuracy

PERF-02.justification: The Integration Service ingests FHIR payloads and buffers them asynchronously via Apache Kafka. This isolates high-throughput ingestion from the synchronous EMR query path, maintaining sub-second screen responsiveness.
sensitivity_points: Kafka partition count and consumer group parallelism
FHIR translation CPU overhead in Camel routes
tradeoffs: Asynchronous ingestion delay versus instantaneous clinical visibility

AVAIL-01.justification: Active-passive synchronous DB replication and Kafka MirrorMaker support zero data loss failover. However, cross-site traffic switching lacks explicit GSLB/DNS orchestration to guarantee full traffic redirection within 60 seconds.
sensitivity_points: Automated database fencing and VIP promotion speed
tradeoffs: Zero data loss via synchronous replication versus write latency overhead

AVAIL-02.justification: Synchronous database replication with automated fencing and PgBouncer minimizes failover disruption. Claim submissions are mediated through transactional handlers and Kafka topics, enabling idempotent retries within 30 seconds.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency key enforcement on claim reprocessing
tradeoffs: Strict transactional idempotency checks versus claim submission throughput

MOD-01.justification: The Payment Gateway Client in Billing Service encapsulates payer integrations using Feign and Resilience4j. The EMR service is completely decoupled via asynchronous events and REST/gRPC boundaries.
sensitivity_points: Standardized internal claim data contract decoupling external protocols
tradeoffs: Custom gateway adapter overhead versus unified internal billing models

MOD-02.justification: Updating a demographic field requires modifications to only three components: Clinical Workspace Module (UI), Patient Admission Component (logic/validation), and PostgreSQL schema. Audit ingestion handles generic payloads seamlessly.
sensitivity_points: Schema migration backwards-compatibility across active-active nodes
tradeoffs: Strict relational schema updates versus schema-less flexibility

SEC-01.justification: Authentication mandates MFA via the external IdP. The Envoy Authentication Filter blocks single-factor access, and the Audit & Telemetry Interceptor streams security violation events immediately to compliance monitoring.
sensitivity_points: Strict token signature validation and revocation check latency
tradeoffs: Mandatory external IdP MFA checks versus user authentication latency

SEC-02.justification: RBAC Middleware validates record access policies, while 100% of read events are captured and offloaded to WORM Object Storage with S3 Object Lock, enforcing tamper-evident 10-year retention.
sensitivity_points: WORM storage retention compliance locking rules
Asynchronous audit logging reliability without dropping read events
tradeoffs: Complete read auditing overhead versus storage consumption and processing cost
